shouldFix.title: The discriminator repair is applied only on the serialized side; on the authorization-record side two of the four classes have no literally resolvable actionSubtype domain, and no other layer closes the gap
evidence: The authorization-record discriminator has its own closed domain. /authorizationRecord/closedMembers/[2] is actionClass with closedValues exactly ['CA-1-HOST-HEAD','CA-2','CA-3','CA-4-HOST'].

The per-class subtype conditionals on that record are keyed to the other vocabulary. /authorizationRecord/closedMembers/[3] is actionSubtype and carries the keys closedValuesWhenCA1, closedValuesWhenCA2, closedValuesWhenCA3, closedValuesWhenCA4. Resolving each legal actionClass value against those keys by literal match gives: CA-2 resolves to closedValuesWhenCA2; CA-3 resolves to closedValuesWhenCA3; CA-1-HOST-HEAD resolves to nothing; CA-4-HOST resolves to nothing. Two of four classes are unmatched.

The same member's nullWhen mixes both vocabularies for one discriminator: 'CA-2 only. A CA-1 record with null subtype is UNCLASSIFIED and DENIED. A CA-3 or CA-4-HOST record with a null or unnamed subtype is UNCLASSIFIED and must resolve DENIED.' CA-1 is not a member of that record's actionClass domain; CA-1-HOST-HEAD is.

The serialized layer does not close the gap, because it carries no per-class subtype binding at all. consentRecordsScopeShape's actionSubtype member has a single flat closedValuesWhenPresent listing all nine subtypes (SPAWN, IN_PROCESS, OUT_OF_ROOT_READ, LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE, KEYCHAIN, PRIVILEGED_PLATFORM_FACILITY, and the three PATH-* values) with no when/nullWhen tying any value to a class.

v9's own new completeness rule stops short of this member. classPredicateDomain.unmatchedSerializedClass requires that 'every legal serialized class must select exactly one byteCap variant and the matching targetIdentity / endpointSet requiredness' — it names byteCap, targetIdentity and endpointSet, and omits actionSubtype. So the artifact adds an explicit no-unmatched-class guarantee on one side of the boundary and leaves two unmatched classes on the other.

No fixture catches the composition. I searched every one of the 24 acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses for subtype coverage: FC-SCOPE-MISMATCH tests an attempt whose class or subtype differs from the record's bound, which is attempt-versus-record and not record-internal legality; FC-ROUND-TRIP tests dropping or relabeling actionSubtype in serialization; FC-C5 and the nullWhen path test an unpopulated subtype. None pins which subtype values are legal for which class, so a record carrying a cross-class subtype is not rejected by any named fixture.

This is the mirror of the defect v9 exists to repair. Frozen Codex HAE7-CX-01, recorded in the subject at /predecessorVerdictFindings/v7/codex/findings/[0], was rated BLOCKER for exactly this shape on the serialized side, and its recorded repair ends 'no legal serialized class is unmatched'. The record side now has two.
shouldFix.impact: For a CA-1-HOST-HEAD or CA-4-HOST authorization record, no layer resolvably states which actionSubtype values are legal: the record's own conditional key does not match its class literal, and the serialized shape accepts any of the nine subtypes. A concrete bad case follows. KEYCHAIN is a CA-3 subtype that the contract holds unexercisable while DR-108 is deferred, gated at FC-KEYCHAIN and FC-NOT-SUFFICIENT, and those gates are written against CA-3. A record carrying actionClass CA-1-HOST-HEAD with actionSubtype KEYCHAIN is excluded by neither layer's literal matching nor by any fixture, so the deferral gate can be routed around by mislabeling the class. The same holds for a CA-4-HOST record carrying a CA-1 or CA-3 subtype.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Apply the domain rule the artifact already states for the scope shape symmetrically to the authorization record. Rename the conditional keys on /authorizationRecord/closedMembers/[3] so each matches a literal of that record's own actionClass domain (closedValuesWhenCA1HostHead and closedValuesWhenCA4Host, or an explicit per-class map keyed by the four record literals), and correct the nullWhen prose so 'A CA-1 record' reads 'A CA-1-HOST-HEAD record'. Then close the serialized side by either giving consentRecordsScopeShape's actionSubtype a per-class binding over CA-1/CA-2/CA-3/CA-4 or extending classPredicateDomain.unmatchedSerializedClass to require that every legal serialized class also select its matching actionSubtype domain. Adding a fixture that rejects a cross-class subtype, for example CA-1 with KEYCHAIN, would make the binding testable; no current fixture does.

advisories.title: The authorityClaim's containment statement for the record vocabulary is not literally accurate
advisories.observation: authorityClaim states that authorization-record vocabulary 'remains only at authorizationRecord.actionClass, doctorV4FieldMapping, and effectCommit'. I enumerated all 14 occurrences of CA-1-HOST-HEAD or CA-4-HOST in the subject. Three fall inside authorizationRecord but outside its actionClass member: closedMembers[3].nullWhen (actionSubtype), closedMembers[5].semantics (admittedManifestDigest, 'For CA-1-HOST-HEAD'), and closedMembers[11].semantics (endpointSet, 'For CA-4-HOST'). Three more are prohibition, fixture or history statements that must name the literals in order to forbid or record them, at classPredicateDomain.rule, FC-BOUND-SHAPE.passProperty and predecessorVerdictFindings.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The occurrences in closedMembers[5] and [11] are correct usage: they describe authorization-record members and the record vocabulary is the right vocabulary there. The prohibition and history statements are unavoidable. Only the containment sentence is imprecise, and the substantive consequence of the closedMembers[3] case is already carried as CLAUDE-HEA9-S1.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. Widen the sentence to 'authorizationRecord, doctorV4FieldMapping and effectCommit, plus the prohibition and fixture statements that name them'.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. The claimed repair itself is sound and I could not break it: every scope predicate uses the serialized domain, coverage over the four classes is total, the retired translation map survives intact at its new home, and a named fixture now fails any predicate using the forbidden literals. Custody is clean on every pin including the recorded v8 that had been edited in the working tree earlier, all 29 live recordedInputs digests reproduce, the D-032 section reproduces at the stated line range despite append-only COORD growth, and every authority guardrail holds with three new disclaimers added in v9. The finding is that the repair is one-sided: the artifact declares a closed discriminator domain and a no-unmatched-class guarantee for the serialized shape, then leaves the authorization record's own actionSubtype conditionals keyed to literals absent from that record's actionClass domain, so CA-1-HOST-HEAD and CA-4-HOST records have no resolvable subtype domain at either layer and no fixture catches a cross-class subtype. That is the same defect class as the BLOCKER this generation exists to repair, and it has a concrete consequence for the deferred KEYCHAIN gate. It is repairable by renaming keys and extending one completeness rule; it does not require redesign.
